title: Moment-finder list for both texts
subject: English Literature
source: Written for english-literature/y11 lesson 51 (Moment-finder list for both texts (pupil PDF))
intro: Lesson 51: Optional clinic before Component 2 (Wed 19 May). Read the ideas from the lesson, then do the tasks.

panels.title: How the clinic works
points: Optional: bring one question and your clean texts

parts.text: Read both questions for each text
Choose the one with the most moments you know
List three moments with page numbers

parts.label: Why it works
parts.text: After five minutes: question chosen, three moments located, thesis written.

keywords.def: an optional session to ask questions and practise
a clean copy of the text is allowed
a technique used in plays, such as stage directions or dramatic irony

questions.q: Post your one question here and note the answer
questions.a: A question and a clear answer.

questions.q: Moment-finding race: locate five moments in each clean text
Core: in the portal response box, write a thesis and three located moments for one question on each text (5 minutes each)
questions.a: Two theses with three located moments each.

questions.q: Extend: add one context point to each thesis
questions.a: Two context points linked to purpose.

questions.q: Stretch: write the first two sentences of one answer
Which thesis is strongest for 'How does Priestley present Sheila?'
options: Sheila is a character in the play.
Sheila is the daughter of Mr Birling.
Priestley uses Sheila to show that the young can learn responsibility, unlike their parents.
questions.a: C) Priestley uses Sheila to show that the young can learn responsibility, unlike their parents.. An arguable claim about the writer's purpose.

questions.q: How do you feel about Wednesday?
Answer the ponder: which moment would you check?
questions.a: A named moment with a reason.
